reasoning_traces.think:
The paper establishes a duality between proper scoring rules and forecast pooling methods. For any strictly convex scoring rule G with exposure function g, the Quality Assurance (QA) pool minimizes the weighted average Bregman divergence to expert forecasts. This is expressed mathematically as p* = argmin_x Σw_i D_G(x ∥ p_i). The exposure function g(p) = ∇G(p) links the scoring rule to the pooling operator. Linear pooling emerges from the quadratic rule (g_quad(x) = 2x), while log pooling arises from the logarithmic rule (g_log(x) = ln(x+1)). These mappings ensure that the resulting pool is max-min optimal, meaning it minimizes the worst-case loss across all experts. Furthermore, the score function s(p;j) = G(p) + ⟨g(p), δ_j - p⟩ provides a dual characterization of the scoring rule’s behavior. Concavity of the score in weights (WS_j(w)) allows for regret-optimal online learning using gradient descent. The regret bound O(√T) holds under adversarial conditions, ensuring robustness. Failure modes include misalignment between scoring rule and pooling operator, which leads to non-concave score functions and thus poor learning dynamics.
